searchText: Hey, update from Prysm: **DONE:** - Prysm is now able to start at Deneb and activate PeerDAS with the Electra fork. Prysm is able to sync from genesis up to the head after the peerDAS activation. (Had some issues with the pre/post peerDAS interface when syncing.) **TO DO before the next devnet:** - Implement https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832 - Activate PeerDAS at Fulu instead of Electra How implementers are confortable with the current state of [3382](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832)? There is at least 3 fixing, not yet merged PRs following up [3382](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832): - https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4060, - https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4062, and - https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4059 <== Test vectors. I'm wondering if [3382](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832) was not merged too early, and if, as it does not bring any real functional change, we should skip it (at least until everything is cleaned up) for the next devnet. Sorry for making things blocked. This https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4063 will fix the test vectors. we've removed `goomy_blob` from the latest ethereum-package version. Instead, there is `spamoor_blob` now, which supports the same features and works more reliable 🙂 optional parameters for fine-tuning: ``` spamoor_blob_params: throughput: 3 # Transaction throughput per slot max_blobs: 2 # Maximum number of blobs per transaction max_pending: 6 # Max pending blob transactions ``` oh, replied to the wrong message.. this was for <@531934490826768418> related to goomy problems 🙂 On a statistical sample of 2 out of 2, it seems there is no issues any more with spamoor.

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
Hey, update from Prysm:
**DONE:**
- Prysm is now able to start at Deneb and activate PeerDAS with the Electra fork. Prysm is able to sync from genesis up to the head after the peerDAS activation. (Had some issues with the pre/post peerDAS interface when syncing.)

**TO DO before the next devnet:** 
- Implement https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832
- Activate PeerDAS at Fulu instead of Electra

excerpts.author: manunlp
excerpts.content:
How implementers are confortable with the current state of [3382](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832)?

There is at least 3 fixing, not yet merged PRs following up [3382](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832):
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4060, 
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4062, and
- https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4059 <== Test vectors.

I'm wondering if [3382](https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/3832) was not merged too early, and if, as it does not bring any real functional change, we should skip it (at least until everything is cleaned up) for the next devnet.

excerpts.author: popef
excerpts.content: Sorry for making things blocked. This https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/pull/4063 will fix the test vectors.

excerpts.author: pk910
excerpts.content:
we've removed `goomy_blob` from the latest ethereum-package version.
Instead, there is `spamoor_blob` now, which supports the same features and works more reliable 🙂

optional parameters for fine-tuning:
```
spamoor_blob_params:
  throughput: 3   # Transaction throughput per slot
  max_blobs: 2    # Maximum number of blobs per transaction
  max_pending: 6  # Max pending blob transactions
```
